analysis.title: Goldman: "Demand For Compute Can Grow Exponentially, But The Capital To Finance It Cannot"
key_insights: Goldman EMEA delta-one head Rich Privorotsky argues the AI trade's constraint has shifted from demand to financing: demand for compute can grow exponentially but the capital to finance it cannot. He says the widening in credit across the AI vertical is a warning.

Wednesday's hot CPI was the trigger. Core rose 0.33% against a 0.2% consensus. Goldman economists raised their September core PCE estimate to 0.32% m/m (3.09% y/y) and said the report raises the probability of an October hike.

Market pricing after the close was 35% odds of an October hike and 87% for December. The S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94 and the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.02%, the first -1% SPX / -2% NDX day since late July. Bonds rallied anyway, which the report reads as the market expecting hikes to break something.

Privorotsky says the pain trade was long AI / short bonds and both sides are now unwinding. Credit concerns have entered the AI spending equilibrium, and the market is reading this as a growth shock. Overnight the 10Y yield fell 10bps to 5.08% and October hike odds slid to about 30% from a 58% intraday peak.

Credit led the selloff. Goldman's global neocloud basket is down 20% in five sessions, which Privorotsky calls roughly a 1st-percentile move over ten years. Hyperscaler IG spreads widened another 7.4bp last week. He frames crowding out as showing up through the marginal borrower, the leveraged neocloud.

CoreWeave unsecured bonds traded below 80 cents with yields above 15%. Goldman's Asia desk says its 2032 debt, bought at par four months ago, trades below 78c, with CDS pricing over a 50% chance of default within 5 years. CDS reached a record 1,117bps (about 63% implied 5-year default odds) and bonds fell a third straight day to a 16.1% yield to worst. Spillover hit Nebius and Oracle equity and credit.

Gartner forecasts that over 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations by 2030. It estimates AI data center owners need $8.5 trillion of cumulative revenue through 2030 to cover capex, financing costs and a 12% return, against no more than $3.6 trillion forecast. ZeroHedge computes the gap at roughly $4.9 trillion. Gartner puts more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending at risk of impairment by end-2030.

Privorotsky says token consumption still surprises to the upside, but the equilibrium increasingly favors owners of powered capacity and strong balance sheets over leveraged middlemen. Hyperscalers can wait for demand to catch up, while a company whose bonds yield 16% cannot.

Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam notes spreads are now under 15% of the all-in yield on the USD IG index versus 45% in 2019-21. That makes parts of corporate credit a quasi-rates product, so AI debt trades on the Fed's path.

Goldman FX vol head Praneet Shah revives R**, the rate level above which financial stability and credit concerns start to bite. He says the AI capex ecosystem may be nearing that level and that the bull flattening is consistent with it being tested. Stress shows in credit, equities (Nasdaq and KOSPI selling off together), rates and FX (USD, KRW, TWD weaker, EUR, CHF, JPY stronger).
Shah calls the equities-lower / yields-lower tail under-hedged by clients and recommends USDJPY downside via digital puts.

The selloff spread to the AI supply chain. KOSPI fell 7.57% and tripped Level-1 circuit breakers for the first time since July 29 on its 7th straight down day. SK Hynix is 57% and Samsung 40% off their peaks. Foreigners sold $2,748mn on the day while Korean retail bought $1,009mn. The Nikkei had its biggest drop since March (2.7-sigma) and Asia IG sovereign spreads widened 5-8bp.

In the US, CDX 5Y HY spreads hit a 6-month high with CoreWeave contagion cited as a catalyst. GS's HY Debt Sensitive basket fell 4.9% and the Russell 2000 fell 1.9%. Russell 2000 futures open interest rose $1.8 billion, the largest one-day rise of 2026 excluding rolls, with hedge fund shorting likely and an unidentified buyer on the other side.

Goldman's derivatives desk (Adrien Simonet) was pitching long vol on the morning of the selloff. The average 1-year implied vol percentile across its AI basket was 6%, with NVDA at the 1st percentile and TSM at the 0th, driven by vega supply from structured retail products. Indices then realized more than 2x the implied straddle, vol-of-vol rose sharply and dealers are now shorter gamma.

Goldman's reassurance side: Privorotsky thinks the market overreacted in pockets, discretionary nets are low, and stable lower rates would improve the equation. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to $52.3-54.3bn vs a $50.35bn Street and VAT posted organic orders up 188% with a record 1.9x book-to-bill. TSMC kept 2026 capex unchanged at $60-64bn, which disappointed bulls wanting a raise.

Regional desks say the flush has not happened. GS Korea saw no concentrated degrossing or capitulation in memory, GS Japan saw degrossing rather than defensive rotation, and GS US derivatives sees the market cutting the right tail off the AI trade rather than panicking.

ZeroHedge's own take is that the demand case does not depend on rates but the financing case does. With the Fed still priced for an 87% chance of a December hike, the bounce case reduces to rates needing to fall. A Warsh speech is the next checkpoint.

sector_views.rationale: Leveraged middlemen face rising financing costs. The equilibrium favors owners of powered capacity and strong balance sheets, and Gartner expects over 80% of neoclouds to cease independent operations by 2030.
GS's HY Debt Sensitive basket fell 4.9% and the Russell 2000 fell 1.9% as HY spreads hit a 6-month high on CoreWeave contagion.
SOX fell 4.5% and KOSPI fell 7.57%, but regional desks saw degrossing rather than capitulation and demand data from TSMC and VAT remains strong.

cross_bank_references: Which, for those keeping score, is exactly the shape BofA's derivatives team said the AI unwind would take (Oct 15): stocks and yields tumbling.
Goldman's trading desks and Gartner reached the same conclusion on AI returns using 12-15% hurdles.
Gartner's report expresses the view that much of the sector's planned investment may struggle to earn an adequate return (cited by Goldman's Johnstone).

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is intact. Token consumption keeps surprising to the upside, TSMC guided Q4 revenue above the Street, VAT orders rose 188%, discretionary nets are low and positioning, valuations and rates are moving in a more supportive direction. If rates stabilize lower the financing equation improves (Privorotsky).
tension_points.bear_case: Financing capacity cannot keep up. Neocloud basket down 20% in five days, CoreWeave bonds distressed with CDS pricing over 50% default odds, hyperscaler spreads wider, HY at 6-month wides, and Gartner sees an AI revenue gap of about $4.9 trillion against capex and a 12% return hurdle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates failing to stabilize lower while the Fed is still priced for an 87% chance of a December hike, or yields moving above the R** level Shah says may already be tested.

tension_points.bull_case: Regional desks say there was no concentrated degrossing or capitulation in Korea, Japan was not panicky, and the market is cutting the right tail of the AI trade rather than panicking.
tension_points.bear_case: A real flush has not yet happened, so the unwind may continue. Credit stress is spreading across Asia IG, US HY and small caps, and dealers are short gamma.
